target.role: fresh outward saturation test for a distinct GROOVE OVER NOISE function
target.position: outside all frozen and protected regions; placement selected only after belonging
target.purpose: test whether cross-rhythmic dub-space material reveals a lawful new function rather than another occupied groove-development, re-entry, immersion, or release role

explorationReceipt.scope: approximately 82 named track and release listings across 24 official release, label, retailer, catalogue, and bounded query pages screened across all three required source families

currentReleases: 2026-06-01 through 2026-08-14 window; approximately 31 named tracks across nine official release pages and four bounded searches
adjacentAndEmerging: Approximately 29 named tracks across eight official artist or label pages and four bounded searches emphasizing half-time weight, dub space, restrained percussion, broken rhythm, and slow release
Official Livity Sound Terrain Scatter EP: https://forestdrivewest.bandcamp.com/album/scatter-ep
overlookedCatalogue: Approximately 22 named tracks across seven official catalogue pages and four bounded searches for earlier dub, half-time, reduced-percussion, and asymmetrical material

exclusions: Every lead and candidate in prior immutable requests through 2026-08-13 was excluded, including Reger, Joves, Advanced Human, Dillect, Developer, VNNN., Orion, pranch, GI-RO47, Lizoto and Sabrj.
All 26 ledger identities, durable rejected entries, frozen Session 4 material, protected opening and ending, and untriggered PARKED revisit entries were excluded.

Current-release material was excluded when exact-track behaviour was undocumented, when the described role required the protected ending, or when descriptions emphasized abrasion, confrontation, peak-time pressure, emotional catharsis, obvious melody, or impact.

Terrain — Barossa Dub and Hive revealed genuinely different half-time or slow-release functions but were excluded before Spotify resolution because exact retailer metadata places them at 80 and 110 BPM, leaving no canonical neighbour within the required 0–4 BPM range.

RÖM alternatives were excluded when they were explicitly downtempo, ceremonial, densely percussive, or built around a field-recorded voice; Whispering Dub alone retained a plausible cross-rhythmic hypothesis despite an explicit voice-attention risk.

Overlooked catalogue material was excluded when it duplicated an existing dub-development or release role, supplied only release-level terminology, or leaned on breakbeat energy, melodic climax, distortion, hooks, or genre reputation rather than exact behavioural evidence.
No lead was admitted for novelty, popularity, duration, BPM, artist reputation, label reputation, or quota completion.
explorationReceipt.evidenceLimit: Official exact-track descriptions and external identity metadata only; no Spotify audio analysis, no raw-audio measurement, and no candidate-specific listener report.

leads.fitHypothesis: The official exact-track description combines dub space, half-time weight and meditation, which could reveal a distinct cross-rhythmic release function; the same description foregrounds pressure shifts and whispered voices, so playlist belonging, attention continuity, exact tempo and both placements remain uncertain.

evidence.attributedDescription: The official RÖM release notes describe Whispering Dub as a pressure-shifting meditation where dub space and halftime weight meet, with whispers bleeding through cavernous reverb.
evidence.craftConvention: A cross-rhythmic dub-space track can create a meaningful partial release only when its pulse remains compatible and its voice or pressure changes do not pull attention out of the long-form journey.
